review_notes: I read the whole file. I did not compile any rewrite, so each rewrite below is checked against hypotheses and declaration order only. I confirmed all three candidates and added one missed finding.

claims.reason: The same card argument appears four times: two distinct maximal triangles cannot share 3 vertices. In each copy the intersection has card 3, so it equals both T and U by `eq_of_subset_of_card_le`, a contradiction. The copies are at 435, 468, 576 and 725 (`hcard` at 725 in `triangle_inter_eq_edge`). All four are stated with `T U : M.Triangle` and a hypothesis `T.1 ≠ U.1` (or `U.1 ≠ T.1`), so a single lemma covers them. At 576 the order is `U.1 ∩ T.1` and the hypothesis is `huData.1 : U.1 ≠ T.1`, so instantiating with `T := U, U := T` works. No dependency cycle arises: the lemma needs only `card_triangle`, and `triangle_inter` is not needed. The duplicated tail (`triangle_inter` rewrite followed by the card-≤-2 disjointness lemma) is also verbatim in `disjoint_interior_triangleCarrier_edgeCarrier` and `disjoint_interior_triangleCarrier_triangleCarrier`. The optional second step is sound but secondary: prove the edge version from the triangle version by `Disjoint.mono_right` with `convexHull_mono`. That needs the triangle version moved earlier and the `T.1 = U.1` branch kept.
claims.shared_lemma:
theorem card_inter_triangle_le_two {T U : M.Triangle} (hne : T.1 ≠ U.1) : (T.1 ∩ U.1 : Finset M.Vertex).card ≤ 2 := by
  by_contra h
  have h3 : (T.1 ∩ U.1).card = 3 := by
    have := Finset.card_le_card (Finset.inter_subset_left : T.1 ∩ U.1 ⊆ T.1)
    rw [M.card_triangle T.1 T.2] at this; omega
  have hT : T.1 ∩ U.1 = T.1 := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le Finset.inter_subset_left (by rw [h3, M.card_triangle T.1 T.2])
  have hU : T.1 ∩ U.1 = U.1 := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le Finset.inter_subset_right (by rw [h3, M.card_triangle U.1 U.2])
  exact hne (hT.symm.trans hU)
rewritten_uses: disjoint_interior_triangleCarrier_triangleCarrier: `have hInterCard := M.card_inter_triangle_le_two hne`, then the unchanged `rw [Set.disjoint_left]; intro p hpT hpU; ...` tail.
triangle_inter_eq_edge: `have hcard := M.card_inter_triangle_le_two hTU`, followed by the existing `symm; exact Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le heInter ...`.
disjoint_interior_triangleCarrier_edgeCarrier: in the `¬ T.1 = U.1` branch use `M.card_inter_triangle_le_two hTU` for `hInterCard`.

claims.reason: `edgeCarrier_diff_vertices_subset_interior_support` (1387) proves that a non-endpoint point of a non-incidence-one edge lies in `interior support`. The proof takes a second incident triangle by the `hother` singleton argument, applies the shared-edge interior lemma, shows the union lies in the support, and applies `interior_mono`. Both later proofs redo exactly this. In `exists_boundaryEdge_through_frontier_point` (1427; `hother` at 1448) the contradiction hypothesis `hne : ¬ card = 1` gives `¬IsBoundaryEdge e`, because `heEdges` is already in hand. The point `p` avoids all vertices, so it avoids the edge endpoints. In `vertex_mem_triangle_of_frontier_not_mem_boundaryEdges` (1542; `hother` at 1573) the `¬IsBoundaryEdge e` branch has `hvNotVertices : ¬ position v ∈ position '' e` and `hvEdge`, exactly what the lemma needs (with `ht := T.2`). Both conclusions are `x ∈ interior support` against `x ∈ frontier support` via `disjoint_interior_frontier`. The existing lemma precedes both uses, so there is no cycle. The hypotheses match, so the replacement is real reuse. The optional `triangleCarrier_union_subset_support` helper is a minor extra: the union-subset block recurs at 1416, 1472 and 1591.

claims.reason: This is the weakest of the three, because the simplex-membership proof is short API boilerplate. It is still justified. The block `e ∈ edges` → `mem_biUnion` → `mem_faces_iff` with `card_pos` is repeated for `e` and `f` in `edge_eq_of_nonvertex_mem_edgeCarriers` (857) and again in `edgeCarrier_inter_edgeCarrier` (915). It appears a fifth time in `vertex_mem_edge_of_position_mem_edgeCarrier` (933). Also `edgeCarrier_inter_edgeCarrier`'s statement is verbatim the `hface` that `edge_eq_of_nonvertex_mem_edgeCarriers` rebuilds by hand; that lemma is simply declared after it and never used. A `mem_simplexes_of_mem_edges` helper plus moving `edgeCarrier_inter_edgeCarrier` earlier removes about 20 lines from `edge_eq...`. The hypotheses match: `card_of_mem_edges` gives `card = 2`, so `card_pos` holds, and no cycle arises. `edge_subset_of_nonvertex_mem_triangleCarrier` builds `heSimplex` differently, from a given `e ⊆ t`, so it is not clearly covered.
claims.shared_lemma:
theorem mem_simplexes_of_mem_edges {e : Finset M.Vertex} (he : e ∈ M.edges) : e ∈ M.toPlaneComplex.simplexes := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht, het⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp he
  have hd := Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp het
  exact M.mem_faces_iff.mpr ⟨Finset.card_pos.mp (by rw [hd.2]; omega), t, ht, hd.1⟩

missed_findings.problem: Two proofs repeat a nontrivial argument: a point in the convex hull of the positions of a vertex set of card ≤ 1 is a vertex position. The case split on the empty set versus a nonempty set is the same in both. The singleton case is also the same: a vertex `v`, then uniqueness via a two-element subset whose card exceeds 1, then `hull {position v} = {position v}`. The first copy is at 887–906, in `edge_eq_of_nonvertex_mem_edgeCarriers`, which ends by contradicting `hpv`. The second is at 1051–1070, in `edge_subset_of_nonvertex_mem_triangleCarrier` (`hcardCommon`, `hsingleton`, `hpEq`). It also ends by contradicting `hpv`. The third, in `vertex_mem_edge_of_position_mem_edgeCarrier`, covers only the empty case.
missed_findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem exists_vertex_of_mem_hull_of_card_le_one {s : Finset M.Vertex} {p : Plane} (hs : s.card ≤ 1) (hp : p ∈ convexHull ℝ (M.position '' (s : Set M.Vertex))) : ∃ v, p = M.position v`. Proof: use `Finset.card_le_one_iff_subsingleton`/`card_le_one`, or `eq_empty_or_nonempty` plus `eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem`. Then `convexHull_empty` or `convexHull_singleton` finishes. Use in the first proof: `obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := M.exists_vertex_of_mem_hull_of_card_le_one hsmall hpInter; exact hpv v hv`. Use in the second: `obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := M.exists_vertex_of_mem_hull_of_card_le_one hcardCommon hpCommon; exact hpv v hv`.
